coach_message: Welcome to the team! I have designed a balanced 5-lesson plan focused on elevating your one-handed backhand and sharpening your all-around baseline game so you can shine in your upcoming social matches. I'll check in Monday, Wednesday, Saturday at 18:00 UTC.

nodes.title: One-Handed Backhand Contact
tips: Use an Eastern backhand grip with your top knuckle on the top bevel.
Turn your shoulders early using your non-dominant hand on the racket throat.
Lock your wrist at impact well in front of your lead hip.

drill_spec.title: Impact Point Wall Press
drill_spec.instruction: Place racket against a wall at ideal contact height, holding straight-arm posture for 5 seconds.

nodes.title: Modern Forehand Extension
tips: Unit turn with both hands on the racket as the ball crosses the net.
Drop the racket head below the ball to generate natural topspin.
Extend through the contact zone before wrapping the follow-through.

drill_spec.title: Self-Drop Extension Drill
drill_spec.instruction: Drop ball 2 feet in front; step forward and drive through contact with relaxed elbow extension.

nodes.title: First Serve Trophy Pose
tips: Release the ball with a straight tossing arm to a consistent peak.
Load weight into your back leg while dropping the racket into the trophy position.
Reach up fully to strike the ball at the highest comfortable point.

drill_spec.title: Trophy Pose Hold & Reach
drill_spec.instruction: Toss, freeze 2 seconds in the trophy pose with bent knees and tossing arm straight up, then drive up to full reach.

nodes.title: One-Handed Backhand Drive
tips: Step across with your front foot to close your stance and build momentum.
Pull your non-dominant arm backward at contact to keep your chest from opening.
Finish high with the racket face pointing skyward for depth.

drill_spec.title: Impact Point Wall Press
drill_spec.instruction: Place racket against a wall at ideal contact height, holding straight-arm posture for 5 seconds.

nodes.title: Social Match Baseline Patterns
tips: Direct your first serve toward the opponent's backhand to start the point on offense.
Use cross-court one-handed backhands to maintain high-percentage rally tolerance.
Look for short replies to step inside the baseline and attack with your forehand.
